name: Cutting Room Floor
author: neostryder
description:
Brings back Angband features that later versions dropped, and content upstream wrote but never switched on, as opt-in content. The base game stays faithful to Angband 4.2.6: nothing changes unless you switch a toggle on, and every toggle defaults to off.

Each one has its own toggle, so you can pick just the ones you want.

sections.title: Classic arcane books
sections.description: Restores the nine arcane books for Mage, Rogue and Ranger. Your character starts with the first book. Nine books take more pack space than the current set.

sections.title: Classic prayer books
sections.description: Restores the nine prayer books for Priest and Paladin. Your character starts with the first book. Nine books take more pack space than the current set.

sections.title: Classic class chassis
sections.description: Restores the historical experience penalties, skills and hit dice for the five classic spellcasting classes.

sections.title: Restore Teleport Other (Priest, Paladin, Ranger)
sections.description: Angband 4.1.3, the last official release before the 4.2.0 spellbook rewrite, gave every spellcasting class a way to teleport a monster away. Angband 4.2.6 kept it for the Mage and the Rogue and dropped it for everyone else. This adds the same spell, a bolt that teleports the first monster it hits away (farther at higher level), to the Priest, Paladin and Ranger spell lists. Each class's 4.1.3 entry sets the spell's shape, and the Mage's and Rogue's current copies set its price, so a restored spell costs what the spell costs in the game today. The README explains where every value comes from. The Mage's and Rogue's own copies are unchanged.

sections.title: Restore door spiking
sections.description: Angband 3.4.1, the last official release before the 4.0 command rewrite dropped it, let you jam a closed door with an iron spike to make it harder to open. Since then the command has been gone, and the stackable iron spike has had no use and no way into your pack. This restores both: Iron Spikes as an item you can find, and a 'spike' command that uses one to raise the target door's lock strength. The command takes the original j key by default if it is free, and never replaces an existing player or mod binding. The README lists exactly what carried over and what did not.

sections.title: Restore the "of Fury" weapon ego
sections.description: Angband 3.0.6 through 3.2.0 could make a sword, polearm or hafted weapon "of Fury": up to +10 to hit and to damage, two to five points of strength, one or two extra blows and immunity to fear, paid for by aggravating the monsters around you. Upstream switched it off in 2011 by commenting out those three weapon types and left the rest of the record in place, and 4.2.6 still ships it that way. This puts the three types back and changes nothing else, so the ego keeps 4.2.6's own numbers: it appears from depth 50 and is the rarest weapon ego in the game.

sections.title: Restore cut rods, wands and staffs
sections.description: Brings back six magic devices that later versions removed: the rods of Door/Stair Location and Trap Location (last in 4.0.5), the wand of Door Destruction (last in 4.1.3), and the staffs of Trap Location, Door/Stair Location and Object Location (last in 3.0.9). Each one uses an effect the game still has. The rods and the wand keep their original numbers. Angband 3.0.9 wrote the staffs' effects in code rather than data, so they detect over the same area as 4.2's own detection items.

sections.title: Restore cut potions
sections.description: Brings back seven potions that Angband 3.0.9 had and 3.1.0 removed, plus Lose Memories from 4.1.3. Weakness, Stupidity, Naivety, Clumsiness and Sickliness each drain one stat, the same way the base game's other stat drains work, so gaining a level restores it. Lose Memories costs a quarter of current experience unless you have Hold Life; Restore Life Levels restores it. Apple Juice and Water are harmless and feed you a little. The five stat-draining potions appear half as often as they did in 3.0.9, at the same rate as 4.2's Salt Water.

sections.title: Restore cut weapons, armour and diggers
sections.description: Brings back seven items that Angband 3.0.9 had and 3.1.0 removed: the Sabre, the Small Sword, Rusty Chain Mail, Double Chain Mail, the Gnomish Shovel, the Dwarven Shovel and the Dwarven Pick. Angband 4.2 raised body armour values and moved digging to three grades, so the two chain mails take the armour class their 3.0.9 equals have in 4.2, and the diggers take the grade of a 4.2 digger that dug as well. Items that 3.1.0 only renamed, such as the Shadow Cloak (now the Elven Cloak), are already in the game and are not added twice.

sections.title: Restore the deadly potions
sections.description: Brings back three potions that Angband 3.0.9 had and 3.1.0 removed, each one a disaster to drink before you know what it is. Death deals 5000 damage, which kills almost any character. Ruination deals 10d10 damage and drains five stats. Detonations deals 50d20 damage, stuns you badly and leaves a deep cut. They are rare, and appear only from depth 40 (Ruination), 55 (Death) and 60 (Detonations).

sections.title: Restore the monsters cut in 4.2.0
sections.description: Angband 4.2.0 replaced 55 monsters in a pass that made the game's cast fit Tolkien's world: the dark elves, Greek myth such as Medusa, Atlas and the Lernaean Hydra, the ninja and the dagashi, the drider, the black pudding and others. This brings 54 of them back from Angband 4.1.3 with their original numbers, alongside the 4.2 monsters that took their places. Where a 4.2 monster took an old one's depth, speed and hit points exactly, both of the pair appear half as often, so those depths keep their usual mix. Azog, King of the Uruk-Hai stays out, because 4.2 already has Azog under another title.

sections.title: Restore the novices, swordsmen and angels
sections.description: Brings back sixteen monsters from Angband 3.x, alongside the monsters that replaced them. The six novice adventurers gave way to soldiers, cutpurses, acolytes, apprentices, scouts and gallants in 3.3. The Swordsman and the Hardened warrior last appeared in 3.4.1. The angels (Angel, Archangel, Cherub, Seraph and Archon, and the uniques Uriel, Azriel and Gabriel) were replaced by the Maiar in 3.4. All of them keep their 3.x numbers. Crebain is not included, because 4.2's craban is the same bird.

sections.title: Add the Amulet of Amandil (never released)
sections.description: Upstream wrote this artifact in 2011 and left it commented out, and it has stayed that way in every release since, 4.2.6 included. It is a golden amulet found from depth 60 that gives two points of speed, four of searching, resistance to lightning and cold, and protection from fear, blindness, stunning and confusion. This switches the record on with its own numbers. Unlike the rest of this mod, it adds something no released version of Angband had.

sections.title: Restore the bronze dragons
sections.description: Bronze dragons breathed confusion. Angband 3.3 switched them off in 2010 and 4.0 removed confusion as an element, so no release since 3.2.0 has generated one. This brings back the giant bronze dragon fly, the baby, young, mature and ancient bronze dragons, the Great Wyrm of Perplexity, and Bronze Dragon Scale Mail, which breathes confusion when you activate it. Each dragon takes the numbers of the 4.2 gold dragon of its size, scaled by how bronze compared with gold in 3.2.0. Their breath hurts and leaves you confused unless you have protection from confusion.

sections.title: Restore sticky curses
sections.description: Angband 4.0 made a cursed item impossible to take off, and nothing else could be wielded into its slot, until the curse itself was lifted. Angband 4.2 turned curses into runes that come and go freely. This pins the 4.2 curses that answer to 4.0's cursed egos (weakness, clumsiness, dullness, sickliness, vulnerability, teleportation, irritation, annoyance, enveloping and slowness) back onto their items, and brings back the cursed Rings of Woe, Weakness, Stupidity and Aggravate Monster, the Amulet of DOOM and the Staff of Slowness. Curses 4.2 invents beyond those stay free, because 4.2 generates far more curses than 4.0 did.

sections.title: Restore classic uncursing
sections.description: Angband 4.0's Remove Curse took every light curse off every worn item at once and never damaged the item; its stronger form, *Remove Curse*, also lifted heavy curses, and a permanent curse never came off. Angband 4.2's Remove Curse lifts one curse from one chosen item, and a failed attempt can leave the item fragile. This restores the 4.0 behaviour, and the 4.0 chance for an enchant scroll to break a curse: one in four, halved for artifacts.

sections.title: Restore junk items
sections.description: Angband 3.4.1 still had the junk that fills a dungeon: empty bottles, shards of pottery, broken sticks, bones and the skeletons of the creatures that died there, plus the Filthy Rag and the Broken Dagger and Sword. 4.2 dropped them all. This brings back their own item classes (junk, skeleton and bottle) and the records, at the low frequency junk deserves. No tiles ship with them yet.

sections.title: Restore seven ring and amulet flavors
sections.description: In 2013 upstream gave seven ring and amulet looks to artifacts. Ruby, Sapphire and Mithril became the fixed looks of Narya, Vilya and Nenya, Bronze and Golden those of Carlammas and the Necklace of the Dwarves, and Amber and Coral went to the Elfstone and the Evenstar. This adds all seven back as looks an ordinary ring or amulet can have, in their old colours. An unidentified Ruby ring could then be Narya or something ordinary, as it could before 2013.

rules.title: Restore store discounts
rules.description: Angband 3.0.6, the last official release to carry it, sometimes discounted a store item by 10, 25, 50, 75 or 90 percent when it was stocked (10% about 1 time in 25, down to 90% about 1 time in 500; the README cites the exact source). Angband 3.0.8 removed the mechanic and 4.2.6 has never had it back. This restores that roll with the same odds and the same discount sizes.
